A metropolitan statistical area, or MSA, is a type of geographic region used by the United States Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and statistical agencies in defining core urban area for use in applicable programs. Anchored by a major city, the foundational definition of an MSA is a county or counties containing: (1) a city with a population of at least 50,000, or (2) an urbanized area with a population of at least 100,000 (and a total population of at least 75,000). Secondary (lower) definitions of an MSA establish further minimum population density criteria in adjacent commuting zones, along with housing, transport and employment patterns. Full definitions are set forth by the OMB.
Nationwide, there are currently 388 MSAs in the United States and 13 in Puerto Rico. The largest Census-estimated MSA is the Greater New York City Metropolitan Area with over 22.1 million people, and the largest OMB-defined MSA is the Combined Statistical Area (CSA) Greater Los Angeles Area with over 18.6 million people, the second largest MSA.
